screens.purpose: Collect BVN + NIN (11 digits each), verify server-side against NIBSS, and create the draft KycSubmission. Step 1 of 8 in-app.
screens.evidence: Searched "Your BVN and NIN" and "Is this you?" — both found: s12 title "Your BVN and NIN", body "Used once, to confirm you're you. Both must match your official names."; s13 "Is this you?" shows a Name/DOB/Phone confirmation table with "Yes, that's me" / "Re-enter BVN".
screens.why: Direct content match, but the canvas splits BVN/NIN into TWO screens (s12 entry + s13 confirm-details), while the app screen is a single combined form with no post-verification 'Is this you?' confirmation step at all — a real structural gap, not just a style difference.

screens.purpose: Interstitial while the real liveness-verification API call runs server-side; advances on success. Step 4 of 8 in-app.
screens.evidence: Searched "Checking your selfie" and "Done on the spot" — both found verbatim in s16: title "Checking your selfie", body "Done on the spot. If it fails, you just retake it.", spinner, and CTA "Next step · Bank account" (nav.s18).

screens.purpose: Ask whether the investor already has a CHN (CSCS number); collect it if yes, otherwise note one will be auto-assigned. Step 2 of 8 in-app, optional.
screens.evidence: Searched "Do you have a CHN" and "request one for me" (this screen's exact copy) across all 8 canvas .dc.html files — zero matches. Searched "CHN" alone — the only 4 hits are in '06 Account and Support.dc.html', all a read-only display of an already-assigned CHN ('Verified · CHN 0912455', a locked field on the Personal details/Account card), never a collection question. The canvas's own checklist hub (s11) explicitly enumerates exactly 5 steps (BVN&NIN, Documents, Selfie, Bank, Two questions) and CHN collection is not one of them.
screens.why: The new canvas appears to have deliberately dropped CHN collection as a KYC step (matches the 20→4 word-count drop noted in the brief — the 4 remaining mentions are all a post-verification read-only display, not a form). A human must decide: cut this screen (CHN silently auto-assigned, matching canvas's leaner 5-step flow) or keep it as an app-only step with no artboard to restyle against.

screens.purpose: Two SEC-required declarations: PEP (politically exposed person) yes/no with who/position follow-up fields, and 'I trade for myself, with my own money' (blocks Continue if unchecked). Step 7 of 8 in-app.
screens.evidence: Searched "politically exposed" — found in s19 ("Are you, a family member, or a close associate a politically exposed person?"). screens.why: PEP question is a real match on s19, but the app's actual content diverges on two points the canvas doesn't design: the PEP who/position follow-up fields, and the entire second declaration (canvas: broker/NGX-employment question; app: trade-for-self declaration). No 'risk profile'/'profiling' framing found anywhere on this screen or in s19 — confirmed clean on that rule.

screens.evidence: N/A — no build()/UI in this file; it is a state-management class with nothing visual to search the canvas for.

Needs a ruling on whether to split into two canvas-matching screens or keep merged with the app's larger item count.

screens.evidence: Searched "Where do you live?" and "utility bill" — both found in s17 (title "Where do you live?", body "A recent utility bill confirms it, any bill under 3 months old."). s17 ALSO collects street address + State + LGA select fields inline alongside the file upload; the app's utility_bill.dart is upload-only, with no street/state/LGA fields anywhere in this batch.

The app instead has no address-fields screen anywhere in the KYC flow at all — utility_bill.dart is upload-only, and address fields live in the separate pre-KYC onboarding 'personal details' gate (outside this batch, per kyc_intro.dart's own _personalDetailsComplete check). A human should decide whether address collection should move into this KYC step to match the canvas, or stay where the app currently puts it.

kyc_step_sequence.step: Checklist hub (spine of the flow — every step returns here; lists exactly 5 tasks: BVN&NIN, Documents, Selfie, Bank account, Two questions)
Step 1 of 5 — "Is this you?" (confirm name/DOB/phone from BVN records)
Step 2 of 5 — Your documents (pick + photograph one ID type)
Step 2 of 5 (same step as s14) — Address (street/state/LGA) + utility-bill upload
Selfie check (live camera capture in circular frame)
Step 4 of 5 — Add bank account + Direct Cash Settlement opt-in
Verified (success — CTAs: Add money / Browse the market first)

suitability_attachment_point: Attach the suitability quiz immediately after s21 'Verified' (Routes.kycApproved), before its 'Add money'/'Browse the market first' CTAs are allowed to proceed to Home — i.e. as the true last step of the KYC-and-onboarding sequence, gating entry into the rest of the app rather than being wedged into the s10-s19 document-collection steps. Evidence: (1) the app ALREADY wires this exact attachment point today — approved.dart's KMilestoneSheet 'Start investing' button calls context.go(Routes.questionnaire) per a direct, restored 2026-08-24 SEC-compliance product instruction ('please make the suitability mandatory'), so no route restructuring is needed, only restyling s21 to add the gate. (2) The canvas's own s20 'Under review' step is an ASYNC wait (1-2 business days per its copy) with no guarantee the investor is still in the app when it resolves — inserting a synchronous quiz there, or earlier among s10-s19's document-collection steps, would either block on a real KYC-review call or force an investor to answer suitability questions before their identity is even confirmed. s21 'Verified' is the first point after a synchronous, in-session decision is possible. (3) No 'risk profile'/'profiling' framing exists anywhere in the canvas's s10-s21 KYC screens (confirmed via the 'politically exposed'/PEP searches above and a full-text read of s19-s21) — the attachment point introduces the quiz cleanly without inheriting risk-profiling language from the canvas.
